messages.subject: Heywood case
parts:
Hi GSEM users,

I am using GenomicSEM for some traits, and I have come across an issue that was raised in the GSEM wiki page. One of the loading scores in my single common factor model has a loading greater than 1 (1.0114 to be exact). Following the advice on the wiki page i used the usermodel function with the following model:

commonfactor.model<-'F1=~ NA*p1 + p2 + p3 + p4 + p5 + p6 + p7
F1~~1*F1'

Common_Factor_v2 <- usermodel(dev_ldsc, estimation = "DWLS", model = commonfactor.model, CFIcalc = TRUE, std.lv = TRUE, imp_cov = FALSE)

This however did not resolve the issue. Could the >1 loading be caused by something else? 

Any help would be appreciated here.

Pedro

messages.subject: Re: Heywood case
parts:
Hi there, 

Referring to this older post. Good explanation from the authors here.
https://groups.google.com/g/genomic-sem-users/c/x3V5xeKgZ_g

Have you tried to constrain the indicator that has >1 loading and negative residual? Lets say the indicator giving you the problem is p3, then you can do this in your model to constrain the residual variance.
commonfactor.model<-'F1=~ NA*p1 + p2 + p3 + p4 + p5 + p6 + p7

messages.author: 7df5109329109a16
messages.subject: Re: Heywood case
parts:
If your loading for an indicator is greater than 1 and you don't have a negative residual variance then I think you are fine (I have seen these results myself). These results just suggest a high degree of multicollinearity in your data. The negative residual variance is where the issue truly lies because its something that could not exist in the population. 

If others see this, please correct me if I am also misunderstanding these results
